claims.text: Sphere India's situation report 'Extreme Weather Events in India — Assam, Odisha, Gujarat, Kerala and Maharashtra' (dated 2 August 2026, posted to ReliefWeb 3 August 2026): 'India is facing multi-state monsoon emergencies across Assam, Odisha, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Kerala, with Assam and Odisha the worst-affected due to severe flooding, large-scale displacement, and extensive crop and livestock losses.' For Assam: 'As per ASDMA's DRIMS report, 1,78,837 people have been impacted' across 7 districts, 20 revenue circles and 349 villages, with 'No human deaths or missing persons... reported as of 1 August 2026.' Statistical overview for Assam: Inmates in Relief Camp 11,489; Non-Camp Inmates in Distribution Centres 5,569; Relief Camps 61; Relief Distribution Centres 17.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: ReliefWeb's India country page shows no Sphere India situation report or IFRC DREF update newer than the previously recorded 2 August/6 August 2026 editions; the combined national figure (at least 84 deaths, at least 320,456 displaced) remains the freshest citable total.

IFRC's Assam Floods DREF Operation report (6 August 2026), hosted on ReliefWeb, states the Assam floods began 19 July 2026 with rainfall reaching up to 490% above normal in parts of Upper Assam; the emergency peaked 27-28 July with more than 800 villages inundated. Since late July, receding river levels and improving weather have led to gradual improvement, though '1,144,733 people remain affected across eight districts, with floodwaters still impacting 437 villages' as of the report date -- a distinct 'affected' metric from this record's previously recorded displacement figure, so it is not used to overwrite that figure. The report characterizes the crisis as having 'moved beyond its peak' while significant humanitarian and recovery needs persist in the worst-affected areas (Charaideo, Sivasagar, Jorhat).

Re-checked 11 August 2026: direct fetch of ReliefWeb's India country page and the IFRC DREF operation report returned HTTP 403 today. A web search surfaced non-allowlisted wire/press reporting (Associated Press, syndicated via NPR member stations and Washington Post) citing the Assam State Disaster Management Authority for an Assam flood death toll of 100 and roughly 300,000 people in relief camps as of 10 August 2026 -- higher than the 74-death IFRC-sourced figure already on file -- but as of this check that figure has not appeared on an allowlisted government, UN, or Red Cross/Red Crescent source, so it is not adopted into the headline totals; the combined confirmed toll (at least 84 deaths, at least 320,456 displaced) remains unchanged.

Odisha section: 'Odisha continues to face widespread flooding triggered by a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal, affecting 5.93 lakh+ people across 18 districts... with 2,67,301 lakh people evacuated to safer locations as on 31st July.' Statistical overview: Total Population Affected 5.93 lakh (593,000+); Residents Evacuated to safer location 267,301; Relief Camp and free kitchens operational 600+; Causalities [human]: Not reported. Government Response section: 'State government operating 476 relief camps sheltering 1.76 lakh evacuees across 18 districts.'

Gujarat section: 'Heavy rainfall across south, central, and urban Gujarat has triggered severe flooding, affecting 27,856 people who have been relocated from multiple districts including Surat, Navsari, Bharuch, Tapi, Morbi, Surendranagar, Chhota Udepur, and Vadodara.' Statistical overview: Total Population Affected 27,856 Approx.; Residents Relocated to safer location 22,000 Approx.; Causalities: Not reported. Structural damage includes 'the collapse of a 40-metre stretch of the Tapi riverside road in Surat.'

Kerala section: 'Kerala is experiencing severe monsoon conditions marked by intense rainfall, flash floods, and multiple landslides across high-range districts. As of 2 August 2026, at least 7-8 fatalities have been reported across Kottayam, Idukki, Pathanamthitta, Malappuram and Wayanad... The IMD has issued orange alerts for most districts, and authorities have opened 65 relief camps.' 'Heavy rainfall triggered landslides and flash floods, resulting in 7-8 deaths, including four killed in landslides and three children who drowned in rain-related incidents.' Statistical overview lists Causalities: 7; Total Population Affected: Information awaited.

Maharashtra section: 'Continuous heavy rainfall across Maharashtra has triggered flooding in multiple districts, particularly Nagpur, Palghar, Pune, and parts of the Konkan belt... Landslides in Maval and Mulshi have worsened displacement.' Statistical overview: Total Affected Districts 4; Residents Relocated to safer location: 1,155 Approx.; Causalities: 3.

'The national emergency coordination meeting, convened online by Sphere India's Inter-Agency Coordination Committee on 30 July 2026, brought together national NGOs, UN agencies, the Indian Red Cross Society, Inter-Agency Groups (IAGs), Sphere India members and state-level humanitarian partners to review the escalating flood situation across Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Odisha.'

Sphere India's 'Situation Report 2 — Flood Situation in Assam and Mizoram' (dated 18 July 2026, posted to ReliefWeb 19 July 2026): 'Flood conditions continued across Assam on 18 July 2026, with 7 districts affected... A total of 154 villages across 14 revenue circles remain impacted. 21,274 people are affected... No human deaths or missing persons were reported.' This confirms the flooding series began with an earlier Situation Report 1 dated 16 July 2026, establishing the event's onset date.

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch of reliefweb.int/country/ind: Sphere India's Situation Report (2 August 2026) remains the latest multi-state coordination sitrep, with no Situation Report #5 published. A separate 5 August 2026 ReliefWeb report by Humanitarian Aid International states, for Assam alone: 'A total of 87 deaths have been confirmed, and more than 705,000 people have been affected' (period '19 July-present') -- this conflicts sharply with the Assam State Disaster Management Authority figure already on file (no deaths, 178,837 affected, as of 1 August, cited via Sphere India) and is not adopted as the headline figure pending corroboration from an official government or UN-coordinated source; it is noted here as a divergent, unverified claim only.

New authoritative report found 8 August 2026: IFRC's DREF Operation Update No. 1 for 'India: Assam Floods' (DREF operation no. MDRIN029, published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb) states: "The floods have caused extensive damage to homes, livelihoods, and essential infrastructure across Assam. A total of 1,368 houses were fully damaged and 11,066 partially damaged, while more than 74,450 hectares of agricultural land were affected... In addition, 74 flood-related deaths have been reported... On the basis of situation report shared by Chief Minister Office, as of 28 July 2026, the floods had affected 1,144,733 people across 25 districts... The flooding led to large-scale displacement, with nearly 30,000 people evacuated and over 71,000 people accommodated in relief camps at the height of the emergency." This IFRC figure, sourced to the Assam Chief Minister's Office, is more recent and substantially higher than the ASDMA figure relayed by Sphere India already on file (0 deaths, 178,837 affected, as of 1 August) and is now adopted as the current Assam figure, superseding it; despite the overall decline in flood impacts noted by IFRC, 1,144,733 people remain affected across 8 districts as of this report. Combining updated state figures: Assam 74 deaths / ~30,000 evacuated, Odisha 0 deaths / 267,301 evacuated, Gujarat 0 deaths / ~22,000 relocated, Kerala 7 deaths / evacuee count not reported, Maharashtra 3 deaths / ~1,155 relocated -- giving a revised combined total of at least 84 deaths and at least 320,456 people displaced nationwide. No allowlisted source has declared any state's flooding resolved.

description: Heavy monsoon rains through July and early August 2026 have triggered severe, concurrent flooding and landslides across five Indian states — Assam, Odisha, Gujarat, Kerala and Maharashtra — with Assam and Odisha the worst-affected by large-scale displacement and Kerala the hardest-hit by landslide fatalities. Sphere India, the national coalition of humanitarian agencies in India, has coordinated a multi-state response since a national emergency coordination meeting on 30 July 2026, publishing a rolling situation-report series (hosted on ReliefWeb) tracking impact across the five states. Assam's flooding began in mid-July with an initial ReliefWeb situation-report series on Assam and Mizoram from 16 July 2026. New authoritative report found 8 August 2026: IFRC's DREF Operation Update No. 1 for 'India: Assam Floods' (DREF operation no. MDRIN029, published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb) states: "The floods have caused extensive damage to homes, livelihoods, and essential infrastructure across Assam. A total of 1,368 houses were fully damaged and 11,066 partially damaged, while more than 74,450 hectares of agricultural land were affected... In addition, 74 flood-related deaths have been reported... On the basis of situation report shared by Chief Minister Office, as of 28 July 2026, the floods had affected 1,144,733 people across 25 districts... The flooding led to large-scale displacement, with nearly 30,000 people evacuated and over 71,000 people accommodated in relief camps at the height of the emergency." This IFRC figure, sourced to the Assam Chief Minister's Office, is more recent and substantially higher than the ASDMA figure relayed by Sphere India already on file (0 deaths, 178,837 affected, as of 1 August) and is now adopted as the current Assam figure, superseding it; despite the overall decline in flood impacts noted by IFRC, 1,144,733 people remain affected across 8 districts as of this report. Combining updated state figures: Assam 74 deaths / ~30,000 evacuated, Odisha 0 deaths / 267,301 evacuated, Gujarat 0 deaths / ~22,000 relocated, Kerala 7 deaths / evacuee count not reported, Maharashtra 3 deaths / ~1,155 relocated -- giving a revised combined total of at least 84 deaths and at least 320,456 people displaced nationwide. No allowlisted source has declared any state's flooding resolved. Re-checked 9 August 2026: no Sphere India situation report or IFRC DREF update newer than the previously recorded 2 August/6 August 2026 editions could be located on ReliefWeb's India country page; the combined national figure (at least 84 deaths, at least 320,456 displaced) remains the freshest citable total. Re-checked 10 August 2026: IFRC's Assam Floods DREF Operation report (6 August 2026, via ReliefWeb) describes the crisis as having moved beyond its peak, with 1,144,733 people remaining affected across eight districts as flood impacts recede -- a distinct 'affected' metric from the previously recorded displacement figure, retained unchanged pending a directly comparable update. Re-checked 11 August 2026: direct fetch of ReliefWeb's India country page and the IFRC DREF report returned HTTP 403 today. A web search surfaced non-allowlisted wire/press reports (AP via NPR/member stations, Washington Post) citing Assam State Disaster Management Authority figures of the Assam flood death toll reaching 100 as of 10 August 2026 with roughly 300,000 people in relief camps -- this diverges further from the IFRC-sourced Assam figure (74 deaths) already on file, but as with the earlier divergent NGO claim (5 August 2026, not adopted), it has not yet been located on an allowlisted government, UN, or Red Cross/Red Crescent primary source, so it is not adopted into the headline totals. The combined confirmed toll (at least 84 deaths, at least 320,456 displaced) remains the on-file figure pending a citable update.

impact.summary: Sphere India's 'Situation Report — Extreme Weather Events in India' (as of 2 August 2026, hosted on ReliefWeb) reports concurrent monsoon emergencies across five states. Assam: 178,837 people impacted across 7 districts per the Assam State Disaster Management Authority's DRIMS report, with 11,489 people in 61 relief camps plus 5,569 in non-camp distribution centres; no human deaths or missing persons reported as of 1 August 2026. Odisha (worst-hit): more than 593,000 people affected across 18 districts, with 267,301 people evacuated to 476 relief camps; no human casualties reported, though 12 livestock deaths were recorded. Gujarat: 27,856 people displaced (about 22,000 relocated to safer locations) across 6 districts, with a 40-metre stretch of riverside road collapsing in Surat; no deaths reported. Kerala: at least 7-8 deaths (four in landslides, three children drowned) across Kottayam, Idukki, Pathanamthitta, Malappuram and Wayanad districts, with 65 relief camps opened and IMD orange alerts issued. Maharashtra: 3 deaths and about 1,155 people relocated to safer locations across 4 districts (Nagpur, Palghar, Pune, Konkan belt), with landslides in Maval and Mulshi. Combining the states' reported evacuation/relief-camp/relocation figures gives at least 307,514 people displaced; combining Kerala's and Maharashtra's confirmed death tolls gives at least 10 deaths nationwide (Kerala's narrative text cites '7-8' fatalities; this figure uses the report's own statistical-box count of 7). No allowlisted source has declared the flooding contained or resolved, and IMD continued forecasting further heavy rainfall as of the report date. Re-checked 7 August 2026: no newer Sphere India situation report has been published beyond the 2 August 2026 edition already on file. A single NGO report (Humanitarian Aid International, via ReliefWeb, 5 August 2026) claims 87 deaths and 705,000+ affected in Assam alone, sharply diverging from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority's official count (0 deaths, 178,837 affected) relayed by Sphere India; given the conflict with the more authoritative government-sourced figure, this claim is not adopted into the headline totals and is flagged for a follow-up check rather than incorporated. New authoritative report found 8 August 2026: IFRC's DREF Operation Update No. 1 for 'India: Assam Floods' (DREF operation no. MDRIN029, published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb) states: "The floods have caused extensive damage to homes, livelihoods, and essential infrastructure across Assam. A total of 1,368 houses were fully damaged and 11,066 partially damaged, while more than 74,450 hectares of agricultural land were affected... In addition, 74 flood-related deaths have been reported... On the basis of situation report shared by Chief Minister Office, as of 28 July 2026, the floods had affected 1,144,733 people across 25 districts... The flooding led to large-scale displacement, with nearly 30,000 people evacuated and over 71,000 people accommodated in relief camps at the height of the emergency." This IFRC figure, sourced to the Assam Chief Minister's Office, is more recent and substantially higher than the ASDMA figure relayed by Sphere India already on file (0 deaths, 178,837 affected, as of 1 August) and is now adopted as the current Assam figure, superseding it; despite the overall decline in flood impacts noted by IFRC, 1,144,733 people remain affected across 8 districts as of this report. Combining updated state figures: Assam 74 deaths / ~30,000 evacuated, Odisha 0 deaths / 267,301 evacuated, Gujarat 0 deaths / ~22,000 relocated, Kerala 7 deaths / evacuee count not reported, Maharashtra 3 deaths / ~1,155 relocated -- giving a revised combined total of at least 84 deaths and at least 320,456 people displaced nationwide. No allowlisted source has declared any state's flooding resolved. Re-checked 9 August 2026: no Sphere India situation report or IFRC DREF update newer than the previously recorded 2 August/6 August 2026 editions could be located on ReliefWeb's India country page; the combined national figure (at least 84 deaths, at least 320,456 displaced) remains the freshest citable total. Re-checked 10 August 2026: IFRC (via ReliefWeb, 6 August 2026) reports the flood emergency has moved beyond its peak, with 1,144,733 people remaining affected across eight districts; deaths (84) and displaced (320,456) figures are retained unchanged as no directly comparable update was found. Re-checked 11 August 2026: ReliefWeb returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch today. Non-allowlisted wire/press reporting (AP, Washington Post, and NPR member-station syndication) cites the Assam State Disaster Management Authority for an Assam death toll of 100 and roughly 300,000 people in relief camps as of 10 August 2026, which would be higher than the 74-death IFRC-sourced figure already on file, but this has not yet appeared on an allowlisted government, UN, or Red Cross/Red Crescent source and is therefore not adopted into the headline totals, consistent with how the 5 August 2026 divergent claim was handled. The on-file combined figures (84 deaths, 320,456 displaced) are retained unchanged pending a citable update.
